_how_to_use: This is the delegation you SEND, not a description of one. Copy this object, replace the four
<...> placeholders in `task`, `context`, `resources` and `timeframe`, and send it unchanged.
Do NOT compose a delegation from memory and do NOT paraphrase `findings_contract` — the
recorded failure mode across four measured runs is reconstruction: a free-form `criteria`
string went out, `findings_contract:` did not, and the gatherer returned exactly the columns
the payload named and nothing else. Copying is the whole mechanism.
Every key below except the four placeholders is already final. Deleting, shortening or
re-wording `findings_contract` is the defect, including for a question you judged small.
If the delegation tool takes a single string rather than fields, serialise this object and
send it verbatim as that string, with the literal label `findings_contract:` intact.
task: <one sentence: the quality/evaluation question to establish, and for which region/model>
context: <what the user asked, in their words, plus what is already known>
resources: <account alias / region / model ids / invocation log group, account id MASKED as <account>>

findings_contract.output_shape: Return findings ONLY as this table, one row per check, with no prose summary.
findings_contract.table_header: | check-id | Severity | Observed value | Window | Source API | Owning area | AWS doc |
findings_contract.row_count_line: State your row count explicitly as `rows: <M>` on the line immediately above the table, so the count can be reconciled on the return leg.
findings_contract.severities_are_the_catalogs: These severities are `references/checks-evaluation.md`'s. Never improvise one, never round one, and never change one on the return leg.
findings_contract.observed_value_rule: `Observed value` MUST BEGIN with exactly one of the three literal tokens `measured <value>` / `no-datapoints` / `not-queried`. Never a bare number, never `zero`, `none`, `healthy`, `clean`, `no errors`, never a silent omission. There is no fourth token.
findings_contract.source_api_rule: `Source API` names the read-only call that produced the value — `bedrock:ListEvaluationJobs`, `bedrock:GetEvaluationJob`, `bedrock:GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration`, `logs:StartQuery`, `cloudwatch:GetMetricData`, `sagemaker:DescribeTrainingJob`. A value with no API beside it is not a finding.
findings_contract.owning_area_rule: `Owning area` is the area that owns the fix: `output quality` (this skill), `live-failure triage` for an API-error half, `Bedrock invocation logging or access` for logging or access, or `caller` where the fix is in the caller's own request shape.
findings_contract.aws_doc_rule: `AWS doc` MUST be a `https://docs.aws.amazon.com/...` URL. A row without one is not a finding — omitting the citation costs you the row, not the citation.
findings_contract.stop_reason_rule: `stopReason` is NOT a CloudWatch metric. Resolve the log group from `bedrock:GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration` and measure the distribution from the invocation logs. Report BOTH the `end_turn` and the `max_tokens` share, each with the record count it came from, and claim no measurement you did not query.
findings_contract.both_metric_reads: Before reporting that API errors are ruled out as a cause of truncated-looking output, query BOTH `InvocationClientErrors` AND `InvocationServerErrors` in `AWS/Bedrock` over the window and give each its own row. A `filter ispresent(errorCode)` log scan does not support it — invocation logs do not capture pre-flight rejects, so a 0-record scan is a fact about the log, not about the error count.
findings_contract.negative_claims: Never write an unqualified `zero/no <signal>`. A negative belongs in a table row with its token, its window and its source API, or it is `not-queried`.
findings_contract.unconfirmable: Anything you cannot confirm from an AWS API — above all whether evaluation is triggered by a pipeline — comes back as an explicit `cannot be confirmed from AWS APIs` caveat ON ITS ROW, naming where a human would check. Never return a confirmed negative for an absence.
findings_contract.depth_disclosure: If your pass was shallow or partial, say so ON THE ROW and list what a deeper pass would query — unexplained records with their count and share of the window, an unknown onset, a window you did not widen. A shallow pass reported as shallow is a correct answer; a shallow pass reported as unambiguous is not.
findings_contract.read_only: Read-only APIs only. `bedrock:ApplyGuardrail` is never called — it is billable and is not a collection call.
findings_contract.account_id: Never echo a raw AWS account id. Mask the account segment of any ARN as `<account>`.
findings_contract.gaps: Name every gap: what you could not read, and why. A denied or absent signal is recorded, never inferred away.

criteria: <task-specific detail ONLY — never a substitute for findings_contract, which is sent above it unchanged>
